_what: The operating point: the one server command line every measurement and every instruction has to agree with.
_why: It was spelled out in three places that disagreed. On 2026-08-10 the vault page was missing --slot-save-path and --moe-stream-l2 32, while README.md and install.ps1 carried them. Nobody had changed anything wrongly; the copies simply drifted, and a measurement taken against the older line is not comparable to one taken against the newer.
_how_this_is_checked: tools/check_operating_point.py reads the RAW text of README.md and install.ps1 and extracts the flags from it. It must never read a second copy of this file - a checker that compares a manifest against itself is green forever.
_source_of_truth: This file. README.md and install.ps1 are renderings of it for humans; the measurement scripts take their defaults from it.

model._note: Not part of the install: 95.9 GiB and somebody else's artefact.

models._what: Every GGUF a measurement script may point at, by key. tools/model-paths.ps1 reads this; nothing else spells a model path out.
models._why: Measured 2026-08-10: 26 lines across 18 files carried a model path, and 22 of those 26 pointed at files that no longer exist. Not one script was broken by it -- they all take -Model as a parameter, so the dead path is a default nobody notices until a run silently measures the wrong thing, or a model switch has to find 18 files.

operating-point.role: the operating point, and the only model still on disk

iq3-xxs.role: alias of operating-point, for scripts that name the quantisation

q2-k-xl.role: the earlier correctness series; deleted 2026-08-10 to make room for 0731

iq1-s.role: the rung below; measured worthless (emits no function block). Deleted 2026-08-10

mxfp4.role: the 155 GB reference; deleted 2026-08-10. Its chat template survives in manifests/gguf-meta-0.0.6/

drafter-bf16.role: the separate DSpark drafter; deleted 2026-08-10. 0731 carries its draft module inside the checkpoint

sampling._what: What the client and every probe send when nobody says otherwise.
sampling._why: 0.0 is greedy decoding, and greedy is where reasoning models loop: measured 2026-08-07 on a three.js task, the model repeated 'Actually, let me...' inside its reasoning block and never reached the answer. Always taking the single most likely token walks into that attractor and cannot walk back out. DeepSeek specifies 0.6 for this model family. Measurement runs that need byte-identical output pass --temperature 0 explicitly; the interactive default has to be able to finish a turn.
sampling._top_p_note: Not sent at all today, by omission rather than decision -- grep finds no top_p anywhere in tools/ or cli/. The 0731 card recommends temperature 1.0 with top_p 0.95 for agentic use, so this is E11's business, not this stage's.
sampling._measurement_note: temperature 0 in a probe is a MEASUREMENT decision, not a model default: it buys byte-reproducible output. Those literals stay where they are. Only the 0.6 that means 'what we run at' belongs here.

moe_stream_l2._note: Windows reports 63.4 on a 64 GB machine, so a threshold at the nominal size would exclude exactly the configuration this was measured on. install.ps1 prints the flag with a machine-dependent value, so the checker accepts any integer there and only requires the flag itself.

decode_baseline._note: The promise 0.1 has to keep. Length-dependent, so it travels with stall_per_miss_ms below.

not_measured_at_this_operating_point: prefill - every figure on record comes from prompts of 86-103 tokens
quality - the reference series ran at -c 65536 without --jinja
VRAM - documented twice with two different numbers and no run behind either
